notes: Literally 'child of older sibling, child of younger sibling'. When speaking to or about a specific cousin, Thais usually just call them พี่ (older sibling) or น้อง (younger sibling) rather than using this full term.

notes: In Thai, this term covers all children of your parents' siblings regardless of age or gender.

Unlike English, where cousin is a single word, Thai distinguishes between older siblings (pîi) and younger ones (nóng). This phrase combines both to refer collectively to the children of your aunts and uncles.
